10.text: Step two. Reel status now ends with five lines, worked out each time from the reviews. On this repo: fifteen of fifteen recommendations taken, eighty-four of ninety-one calls accepted, and four misses.

11.text: Call A1. The lines' ids are words, not m one to m five, so reel memory own-words says what it prints.

12.text: Call A2. Why you answered in your own words is read from the words: with a condition, unclear, or framed otherwise, with the words shown beside it.

13.text: Call A4. Rewound again after a revision means the same step rewound in two different reviews; rewinds in one sitting count once.

14.text: A3 does not stop: a call counts once, by its first verdict.

15.text: Quick check. In one sitting you rewind step four three times. Does the rewinds line say it was rewound again after a revision?

16.text: Part three: step three, your memory across repos.

17.text: Step three. Reel record now adds a summary line per review to a file in your home folder, and reel memory dash dash you reads it across repos.

18.text: Call A9. That file, you dot jsonl, gets a line each time a review is recorded in a git repo. Each names its reviewer: in this cloud session, git's email, noreply at anthropic dot com, because the page does not send a viewer yet.

19.text: Call A10. Across repos the fifth line is the kinds of call you flagged: a one-line summary cannot say what superseded what.

20.text: Call A15. Where your file cannot be written, as in a sandboxed run, the review is still recorded, and the last line says it is not in your memory.

21.text: Quick check. A sandboxed run records a review, and your home folder is fenced off. What happens?

22.text: Part four: step four, where misses decide what stops.

23.text: Step four. A miss is something a review let through that changed later. Two of this repo's four are recent: decision fifty-six, superseded, and the file tools, reworked. A recent miss stops a call of its kind, whatever its streak.

24.text: Call A11. Recent means shown by one of the last five plans, not a number of days: this repo is worked on in bursts.

25.text: Call A12. None of the misses has tags, so a tagged call matches one by component. Right now that makes decision fifty-six stop every tagged call on the review player: all twenty-two of answer-on-the-video's calls stop, and the file-tools miss stops thirteen of this plan's fifteen.

26.text: Deviation D1. The plan said a part reworked soon after. The build reads that as a step whose walkthrough quick check you disagreed with, not as files changed in git: every plan here touches the player and the CLI, so all would count.

27.text: Quick check. A new call on the review player is tagged close, and close calls have been accepted ten times running. Does it stop?

28.text: Part five: step five, and what ran.

29.text: Step five. Reel status now says a retro is due: six plans, none held yet. Reel retro starts a draft plan that cites its evidence and names the benchmark it is judged by.

30.text: Call A13. A signal is the same thing three times, the same reason, step, component or tag, counted since the last retro.

31.text: Call A14. The retro's folder is named by its date, and its draft passes reel check as written.

32.text: Quick check. You have just held a retro. When does reel status suggest the next one?

33.text: What ran: the memory spec's forty-seven checks, and every spec on a clean copy; four player specs fail there without this change too. The code check found nothing to answer. The narration and visuals are AI-generated. Flag a step or a call, or accept.

01.text: The memory plan is built: all five steps, fifteen calls the plan did not make, and one deviation. That is past the dozen: the plan left too much open, most of all in step four.

02.text: Two of your quick checks on the plan video expected otherwise: nothing reaches your file until dash dash you, and a step rewound twice is a miss. Both stay as planned, with two cheap changes: reel record says what reached your file, and the rewinds line names a step rewound again after a revision.

03.text: Step one. Every review filed from now on carries a stamp: the reviewer, where that name came from, and the reelplanning version.

04.text: Call A5. The stamp is one recorded object, not loose fields, and the same review filed again with another stamp is still one file.

05.text: Call A6. The version is the one that records the review, not the one that built the video: no build writes that down.

06.text: Call A8. Old reviews are migrated unstamped, not stamped with whoever runs the migration: that email and version would be wrong.

07.text: One call here does not stop: A7, the page's viewer is read from the row, once a page sends one.
